title: Peek Mode probe & accessible narrative for dense time-series
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a lightweight ‘peek’ interaction mode for dense time-series views that prioritizes keyboard-first tooltips, an accessible narrative announcer for screen readers, and a low-power rendering fallback (offscreen tiled raster + minimal DOM). Goal is to improve cognitive scanability and a11y for high-density charts while reducing CPU/GPU overhead on constrained devices.

Motivation: Current dense charts present too many focusable targets (one per point) and heavy DOM/paint costs on mobile and low-power devices. Designers and engineers have observed slow hover responses and noisy screen reader output when full per-point announcements are enabled. Peek mode compresses the interaction surface into a small probe area and provides summarized, human-friendly narration that describes range, trend, and notable annotations instead of repeating every datapoint.

Scope: Design component-level specs (probe affordance, compact legend state, keyboard focus behavior, aria-live narrative text, and tooltip content templates) and one reference implementation in the chart library. Work does NOT include server-side aggregation or model-based narration generation — those are future follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Peek affordance: a visible probe handle appears on hover/focus in dense mode; hitting Space/Enter opens a compact tooltip with summary information
Keyboard-first: Tab focuses the probe; arrow keys move the probe in 1, 5, and 30 second increments (configurable); pressing Enter pins the probe
ARIA narrative: aria-live polite region provides a single concise sentence describing the focused window: direction (up/down/flat), min/max with timestamps, and any annotations within the window
Performance: when dense mode is active, offscreen tiled raster technique reduces main-thread paints by at least 40% on a 2017 MacBook Air in internal benchmark
Legend sync: compact legend shows aggregated values (window sum/avg) and exposes an action to expand to per-series details
Graceful fallback: when JS is disabled or screen reader is absent, the chart collapses to a static SVG snapshot with visible legend and static summary text
Docs & examples: Figma spec, design token changes, and one runnable example in storybook added
design_notes: Probe UI should be 8px wide draggable handle with 24px hit area; visual contrast must meet AA on dark and light themes
Tooltip template prioritizes human language: "In the last 5 minutes values trended up from 12→18; peak at 12:07 with annotation: 'deploy'" rather than raw arrays
Compact legend uses color chips plus aggregated metric rows; avoid per-point micro-copy in dense mode
Consider adding an optional 'verbose' toggle for power-users, surfaced in the legend overflow menu
engineering_notes: Reference PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4021 (WIP) implements tiled offscreen canvas + probe input handler
Suggested API: Chart.peekMode = {enabled: boolean, stepMs: [1000,5000,30000], aggregate: 'avg'|'sum'|'minmax' }
Add a rendering flag to skip DOM hover layers and route interactions through a light-weight hit-test index built at tile time
Ensure KV cache and batching are not impacted by additional probe events; throttle probe move events to 20Hz in main runtime
accessibility_notes: Aria-live text must be single-sentence, under 180 characters where possible to avoid aggressive TTS truncation
Screen reader users should receive directional hints only when trend magnitude exceeds configurable sensitivity to avoid noise
Use role="region" with aria-label on the narrations container; label should include chart name and timeframe
Keyboard nav must not expose every datapoint as a focusable element; only the probe handle and legend controls are focusable in dense mode
perf_strategy: Offscreen tiling: pre-render visual tiles to an offscreen canvas and blit visible tiles to a single canvas to minimize layout/paint churn
Hit-test index: build a compact hash grid per tile that maps probe X positions to aggregated values to avoid per-point iteration
Event coalescing: move events from probe are debounced/coalesced at 50ms by default; allow override in props for low-latency use cases
Fallback raster: for low-memory devices fall back to a single raster snapshot of the chart and show a static probe experience
test_plan: Unit: hit-test index accuracy tests across varying densities and edge cases (duplicate timestamps, NaNs)
A11y: NVDA/VoiceOver sweep to validate aria-live sentence composition and keyboard-only navigation
Perf: Lighthouse and custom CPU profile comparing baseline vs peek mode across desktop/mobile simulated devices
E2E: storybook snapshot tests and Cypress tests for probe keyboard flows and legend expansion
